title: On-call handoff notes - Aya Santos 2026-03-03
content:
Shift summary (03/03/2026)

Quick summary:
- Took over from Liam at 08:00 PST.
- Major item: ongoing latency/regional errors impacting model-serving in us-west1 (INC-4521).
- Temporary mitigation in place: traffic split to us-east1 and fallback to model v2-small for low-priority routes.
- No customer-facing SRE page/postmortem yet - incident owner: Samir.

Open incidents / status:
- INC-4521 (high latency + 502s for /v1/generate in us-west1)
  - Observed at ~07:30 PST, spike peaked ~08:15-09:00.
  - Affected routes: /v1/generate (all models) and /v1/chat for prod tenant x-prod.
  - Mitigation: routed 60% of traffic to us-east1, 40% still hitting us-west1 due to DNS TTLs.
  - Temporary model fallback: v2-small deployed on us-west1 and set as compatible fallback in routing policy.
  - Current status: latency improved to ~180-220ms p50 for routed traffic; us-west1 still shows elevated p95 (~1.6s).
  - Next steps: ensure autoscaler is not thrashing, verify kernel failures on GPU nodes (see logs).

Recent actions I took:
- Applied temporary routing change: /routes/prod -> split 60/40 us-east/us-west via console (console change ID: route-split-20260303-aya).
- Triggered rolling restart of serving-pool-us-west-3 (kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-pool-us-west-3) - restarted 3/5 pods successfully; 2 pods stuck Pending (node pressure).
- Opened PR to bump resource requests for serving-pool-us-west to avoid OOM crashes: PR #1482 (link above).
- Notified infra on Slack (#infra) - CPU pressure on us-west1 GPU nodes; possible kernel update last night.

Immediate checks to run (if you pick up this shift):
1) Check incident Jira INC-4521 for the latest timeline and owner notes.
2) Datadog dashboards: runtime-latency, gpu-node-health, k8s-pod-events - focus on us-west1 cluster.
3) kubectl get pods -n serving -l region=us-west1 -o wide; look for CrashLoopBackoff or Pending.
4) kubectl describe node <node-name> on nodes with Pending pods (likely resource/taint issue).
5) Check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and dmesg for kernel GPU errors (if node access permitted).
6) If pods are Pending due to taints, coordinate with infra to drain and re-provision.

Temporary runbook snippets (draft) - commands I used / recommend:
- Check pods: kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=runtime -o custom-columns=NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount --sort-by=.status.phase
- Describe failing pod: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n serving
- Retrieve pod logs (last 2 restarts): kubectl logs <pod> -n serving --previous || kubectl logs <pod> -n serving
- Restart deployment (rolling): kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-pool-us-west-3 -n serving
- Force a quick scale-down/up for a stuck ReplicaSet: kubectl scale deployment serving-pool-us-west-3 --replicas=0 -n serving && sleep 20 && kubectl scale deployment serving-pool-us-west-3 --replicas=3 -n serving
- Check autoscaler status: kubectl get hpa -n serving || check autoscaler controller logs (controller-manager)

Temporary mitigation checklist applied:
- Traffic split configured (console change ID above).
- v2-small fallback enabled for prod routes (need to confirm rollout completed).
- Pager escalations set: if p95 > 1.5s for > 10min, escalate to eng-sre oncall (pager) and infra-SWE.

Things to watch / unresolved items:
- Two pods stuck Pending after restart - looks like node pressure/taint. Infra ticket created (INFRA-2026-77) but not yet actioned.
- Kernel/GPU driver mismatch suspected on some us-west nodes (logs show nvidia: failed to init driver on kernel 5.15.0).
- Model cache warming: after fallback, larger models cold start still causing occasional tail latency spikes. Consider priming cache for hot tenants.
- There is an open follow-up to improve routing TTLs to reduce cross-region bleed - product decision needed.

Notes to self / TODOs (post-shift):
- Follow up with Samir on writing postmortem template + timeline for INC-4521 (owner: Samir Ali).
- Finish PR #1482 for resource bump and get it reviewed by infra (Liam).
- Add a short runbook entry for fallback-to-v2-small (include exact console flags).
- Add a check in SLO monitor: if fallback engaged more than X times/day, trigger long-term investigation.

Customer communications:
- CS/AM notified for x-prod via Jira comment + Slack DM. No public status page update yet - decide with comms if we need a customer-facing note.

Escalation contacts (quick):
- Samir Ali (incident owner) - slack @samir, pager: oncall-sre
- Liam Parker (infra lead) - slack @liam, mobile: +1-555-0123
- Infra team channel: #infra (pings allowed)

Random scratch notes (brain dump):
- If you see GPU kernel init errors: try cordon + drain node, reprovision node image or rollback kernel update.
- For cache warmups: run a synthetic load for top N prompts for tenant x-prod (use scripts/synthetic-warmup.sh)
- Check if any recent model-compiler changes were rolled to us-west1 in last 24h (see PRs in serving-runtime).

End of shift handoff checklist:
- [ ] Confirm INC-4521 updated with latest mitigations and next steps.
- [ ] Confirm two Pending pods issue logged in INFRA queue and owner assigned.
- [ ] Ensure fallback policy still active (do not revert until p95 under 750ms for 30 mins).
- [ ] Post a short summary in #oncall-handoff channel (copy this note).

If anything urgent, page me (Aya) - slack @aya.santos.

---
Document is a working draft - will refine into formal runbook after incident is stable.
